BLOCKER: `core/execution_trail.py` is a new, 302-line substantive module in the shipped root `core/`; it lands only because this same diff amends the reviewed `language-rule.json` exemption list (`allow_new_python`) — a governance change smuggled into a feature diff, against the A6 Go-baseline rule.

The AC-mandated structure is absent: no `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py` thin adapter exists; all logic (store, CLI, rendering, subprocess orchestration) lives in the shipped-root module, so it is not the "thin adapter" the AC requires.

`gate_decisions.py` records stage `f"gate{gate}"`; the decisions it records are the Gate 1.5/2.5 decisions, yielding `gate1.5`/`gate2.5`, which are not in `STAGES` — `record()` raises, the error is swallowed into `_failures.jsonl`, gate1/gate2 never land, and the new blocking gate can never pass.
MAJOR: `REQUIRED_AT_COMPLETION` includes `completion`, but the check runs POST-precheck; the event only exists if status was set via `core.backlog.set_status`. Any completion via direct JSON edit, rollup, dashboard, or migration permanently fails the blocking gate — the AC only requires pre-merge stages here.

`_record_trail` computes `tests`/`code_review` status via `all(...)` over a possibly empty list: a run with no test gates records "tests: pass" with zero rows, fabricating evidence that satisfies the completion requirement.

Failures recorded without an item id (precheck path: `write_failure("precheck", e)`) are never matched by `evaluate` (`ev.get("item") == iid`), so "the completion gate fails" does not hold; backlog/gate0/gate_decisions also emit plain-text warnings instead of the required structured `execution_trail_write_failed` event.
`_failures.jsonl` entries are permanent and unbounded: no acknowledgement/resolution path exists, so one transient lock timeout blocks an item's completion forever.

`order_problems` validates only two pairs (design_review<gate1, diff_review<gate2); the AC's broader "out of order" enforcement is largely unimplemented, and `_stage_events` last-wins on duplicate stages can mask or fabricate ordering.

`execution-trail` is registered in precheck `_GATES` (tier "post") AND manually re-run in `main()` after `_record_trail`; if "post" tier gates execute in the normal loop, the check runs before tests/precheck events exist (spurious failures) and runs twice.
MINOR: The import+record+swallow+warn boilerplate is duplicated verbatim across 5 call sites (backlog.py ×2, gate0_check, gate_decisions, architect_review, precheck) instead of one helper in the trail module.
Trail item regex `^BI-[A-Za-z0-9]+-\d+$` rejects bare `BI-123` ids accepted by backlog `_BARE_BI_RE`; those completions silently degrade to write failures.
`_record_trail` derives ids from the branch name and `record()` never validates the item exists, creating junk trail files for nonexistent items.
`_record_trail` uses `g2._git("merge-base", "develop", "HEAD")` with no `origin/develop` fallback (unlike the check it feeds), silently skipping trail events on fresh clones.
`show`'s usage line always prints numeric totals; the AC's "'not captured' when unavailable" rendering is reduced to a counter, so a fully uncaptured trail shows `0` rather than "not captured".

store-registry adds `trails/<ID>.json` (AC says `<ITEM>`) and only `_failures.jsonl` to the allow list; confirm `engineering/trails/*.json` files are covered or governance checks will flag real trail files.
`refs` (raw `git log --oneline` commit lines) and `tests[].command` are stored unredacted while only summary/actor/error pass through `_redact`.
`record_gate_decision` always records status "pass" regardless of the decision (HOLD/BLOCK included), misrepresenting the gate outcome in the trail.
No test exercises `evaluate`/`main` end-to-end (missing completion stage, failure-sink matching, ordering); only unit helpers are covered.
NIT: `_LAST_USAGE` is a module global; a review rendered from cached evidence or a retried call can attribute a prior call's usage to the wrong item/stage.
`_review_table` re-derives the Gate 1.5/2.5 tables by shelling out to `architect_review.py` (60s timeout) rather than rendering stored evidence, making `show` slow and non-deterministic.
`evaluate` re-reads the whole `_failures.jsonl` once per item (O(items×failures)).
The lock is stolen after a fixed 60s mtime with no owner/PID check; a slow writer can lose its append or duplicate a seq.
`language-rule.json` is fully reformatted in the same diff as the semantic exemption change, obscuring the governance edit in review.
SUMMARY: The trail store and `show` CLI are a sound evidence design, but the diff ships substantive new Python in the shipped `core/` root by self-amending the language-rule exemption and omits the AC's thin-adapter split.
The completion gate as written likely fails every completion: gate1/gate2 are recorded under invalid `gate1.5`/`gate2.5` names, and the `completion` event is required at a pre-merge gate.
Integrity gaps remain: empty test runs recorded as "tests: pass", permanent unresolvable failure-sink entries, item-less failures never failing the gate, and only two ordering rules enforced.
Top risks: governance bypass of the Go baseline, a blocking CI gate that cannot pass, and fabricated or absent evidence satisfying the gate.
